**Macro calendar — midweek refresh**

- **Fire date:** 2026-11-04 (Wednesday, 14:00 ET) · **ISO week:** 2026-W45 **Scope:** Wed Nov 4 (remaining) → Fri Nov 6. Sunday edition's Mon/Tue events are already behind us.

**TL;DR**

- Three Tier 1 prints remain in the week and all three land Friday morning: nonfarm payrolls, the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings.
- There is **no FOMC decision this week** —
- the committee met Oct 27–28 and held at 3.75–4.00% on a 10–2 vote in which Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented **in favour of a 25 bp hike**, so the December 8–9 meeting (with projections) is the live policy event and Friday's payrolls are its main input.
- Today delivered a mixed labour signal that argues for patience rather than alarm:
- ADP private payrolls came in **+86K vs +69K expected** (a clear beat), while ISM services slipped to **54.5 vs 54.8** and S&P final services PMI was revised down to **56.1 from a 57.9 flash**.
- Friday is the risk day of the week; Thursday carries only Tier 2 (claims, productivity).

- **Biggest risk day: Friday, Nov 6** — HIGH_IMPACT_DAY (Tier 1 payrolls triple-header + Michigan sentiment). **Policy backdrop:** hawkish hold, December hike live in the price.
- **No FOMC meeting, no FOMC minutes, no CPI/PPI/PCE/GDP this week** — those land Nov 10 (CPI), Nov 13 (PPI), Nov 18 (Oct minutes) and Dec 8–9 (FOMC + SEP).

**Policy backdrop (why the calendar reads the way it does)**

- **Oct 28 FOMC:** target range held at **3.75–4.00%**, vote **10–2**. Governor Lisa Cook and
- Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, both preferring a **25 bp increase**.
- Statement language: activity "expanding at a strong pace", "inflation remains elevated", "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance".

- **Consequence:** the December 8–9 meeting is priced for a live hike, so **Friday's payrolls are
- hawkishly asymmetric** — a hot NFP or a falling unemployment rate moves December odds directly, while a soft print buys patience.
- Today's +86K ADP is a hawkish tilt into that setup even as the PMIs softened.

- Chair is **Kevin Warsh** (per Oct 28 press conference coverage).
- Context print: Q3 advance GDP was **3.4% annualised** (released Oct 29, cited by Capital
Economics) — growth above trend alongside firm labour demand.
